title: Orthographic Brief — Trace-Paper Construction Document
description: A monospace, all-caps layout that reads like a printed construction document: dimension ticks frame the edges, orthographic wireframes replace decoration, and a two-color ink-on-trace-paper palette enforces a technical rigor absent from generic dark brutalist templates.
philosophy: This template exists for firms that communicate through precision rather than persuasion — where the drawing is the argument, not the backdrop. It refuses gradients, lifestyle imagery, and any element that cannot be traced to a real construction convention. The single warm-tint field, evoking butter-yellow trace paper pinned over a base drawing, is the only concession to atmosphere. It is built for audiences who read dimension lines and contour annotations fluently, and who distrust anything that looks like it came from a generic deck builder.
goodFor: Building proposal presentations to architecture review boards
Urban-planning briefs anchored by site-analysis diagrams
Architecture school portfolio crits and studio reviews
Firm capability decks for institutional or civic procurement panels
avoidFor: Consumer product launches requiring photographic hero imagery
Chart-heavy quarterly reviews with multi-series color-coded data
Audiences unfamiliar with orthographic drawing conventions
Campaigns where brand color systems must remain intact
author: harness

examples.promptCore: The slide feels like a construction document pulled off a studio pin-up wall — austere, deliberate, and quietly authoritative without a single decorative gesture. Composition is asymmetric: sparse orthographic line-work claims the upper field while the identity text anchors the lower register, generating diagonal visual tension across the warm-tinted ground. The mood is institutional and unhurried, projecting the confidence of a practice that lets precision function as rhetoric. Avoid any softness, implied depth, or marks that cannot be traced to a real drafting convention — no vignettes, no texture overlays, nothing that reads as ornament.

examples.layoutNotes: Full-bleed warm-tinted field serves as the base; dimension-tick registration marks run continuously along all four edges, functioning as a border derived from sheet-margin conventions rather than decorative framing. A 12-column grid with roughly 10% outer margin anchors the title block flush-left in the lower half (cols 1–8), with the upper-right quadrant reserved for a ghost-lined orthographic diagram — a site plan or building section rendered at low weight in the secondary ink. Title stacks as one or two all-caps lines; a project number or short descriptor sits below separated by a full-width hairline rule. A sheet-reference notation — number, date, revision mark — occupies the bottom-right corner, mirroring a real title-block cell.

examples.promptCore: The slide feels like a construction document on a light table — sparse, precise, read before admired. Body content is formatted as numbered field notes or annotation callouts rather than decorative bullets, each line carrying the weight of a specification entry. Compositional rhythm is asymmetric: a dense annotation column yields to a spare orthographic diagram, the way a plan sheet balances notes against geometry. Avoid any illustrative or atmospheric mark — every element must trace to a recognizable drawing convention.
